results.note: ingest/registry.py:64-69 adds a model_validator that raises ValueError if any entry.required_bars is None; pydantic wraps this as ValidationError, and the test loads a registry YAML with the field omitted and asserts pytest.raises(ValidationError, match='required_bars').

ingest/compute.py:19-24 checks `received_bars != required_bars` (not >=), so 600 bars against a 500-bar contract raises ValueError('...expected exactly 500 bars, received 600'), which the test asserts via pytest.raises with an exact match string.
Same equality check in compute.py means 499 bars against a 500-bar contract also raises before calculation() is ever called — no partial computation path exists in compute_indicator.

Test packs the result of two in-process calls via struct.pack('!d', ...) and compares both against the hex-encoded output of the same computation run in a freshly spawned `python -c` subprocess, asserting byte-for-byte equality across all three.

Test computes mean over a seeded 500-bar list (asserts value_from_seed == 249.5), then extends the same list object to 600 bars in place — mirroring the prior system's 'grows forever from a 500-bar seed' bug — and asserts compute_indicator on the grown cache now raises rather than returning a drifted number.

Given deterministic gate 'uv run mypy ingest --strict' exit 0. compute.py uses PEP 695 generic syntax (`def compute_indicator[Bar](...)`) and fully-typed signatures consistent with a strict-mypy pass; no // type: ignore or Any leakage in the diff.

note: All five tests in tests/test_bar_slice.py are genuine, assertion-bearing tests exercising the real ingest/registry.py and ingest/compute.py code (not stubs or import-only checks); the exact-equality check in compute_indicator correctly enforces both C2 (too many) and C3 (too few) with the same code path. Minor unrelated churn: SESSION.md and a new project-documents/25_PRD_Acceptance_Protocol.md are included in the diff beyond the four declared files, but this is process documentation, not padding that fakes evidence for this story.
